userStories.title: Weigh complexity in the profile rubric and log plan profile distribution
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Insert complexity-aware eligibility into the shared plan/decompose agent-profile rubric and log the finalized plan's profile distribution.

**Motivation** — Putting complexity into the rubric makes the behaviour the default.

**Approach** — Two small changes, both in `packages/nax`, no new modules and no new exports.

**1. Rubric step.** `OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfileInstruction()` returns five steps instead of four. Steps 1, 2 and the old steps 3 and 4 keep their wording; a new step 3 is inserted after the affinity step:

```text
When agent profiles are listed above, pick exactly ONE profile id per story and set it on the `agentProfileId` field. Apply these steps in order:
1. Eliminate any profile whose weaknesses conflict with the story.
2. Keep profiles whose strengths or affinity cover the story's main job (task type + primary domain).
3. If the story's complexity is `simple` or `medium`, also keep every profile step 1 did not eliminate whose Cost is lower than the Cost of every profile step 2 kept (low < medium < high), even when its affinity does not list the story's task type or domain. If step 2 kept none, keep the lowest-Cost profiles step 1 did not eliminate. Profiles whose Cost is — are ignored by this step, both as candidates and in the comparison.
4. If more than one remains, choose the LOWEST cost profile.
5. If none clearly fit, omit `agentProfileId` entirely — never invent a profile id.
```

The new step never re-admits a profile step 1 eliminated: weaknesses still rule a story out. It only adds profiles strictly cheaper than what step 2 kept, so when every profile shares one cost tier it adds nothing and the affinity filter still decides. It ignores profiles with no `costTier` (rendered `—`): they are never added by this step and play no part in the comparison. For a `simple` or `medium` story, step 5 (omit) is therefore reached only when step 1 eliminated every profile, or when every remaining profile's Cost is `—` and none matched in step 2. For `complex` and `expert` stories the rubric behaves exactly as before. "Cost" refers to the `Cost` column of the capability card table `agentCapabilityCards` already renders from `costTier`, whose values are `low`, `medium` and `high`.

Because both callers append the same static text, the change reaches `nax plan` (`PlanPromptBuilder.build`, via its `agentProfilesSection`) and `nax plan --decompose` (`buildDecomposePromptSync`, via `OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfiles`). The step says "the story's complexity" rather than naming a field because the two output schemas differ: `nax plan` writes `routing.complexity` (`plan-builder.ts`), while decompose writes a top-level `complexity` (`decompose-builder.ts`) that is later stored as `routing.complexity`. Both models produce the value in the same response, so the step applies to both unchanged.

**2. Plan-time distribution log.** `finalizeAndWritePrd` (`src/plan/strategies/persist-prd.ts`) logs one `info` line after `finalizePrdRouting` returns and before the PRD is written:

- stage `"plan"`, message `"agent profile assignment"`
- data `{ storyCount, byProfile, unassigned }`, where `storyCount` is the number of stories counted, `byProfile` maps each `routing.agentProfileId` that names a profile in `args.agentRouting.profiles` to its story count, and `unassigned` counts counted stories whose `routing.agentProfileId` is absent or names no configured profile.
- The counted stories are the finalized PRD's stories, restricted to `args.scope` when a scope is given (decompose adds stories to an existing PRD and only those are counted).
- Counts are taken from the finalized PRD, so a story whose unknown profile id fell back to `routing.agents.default` is counted under the default profile's id. With no default, `finalizePrdRouting` leaves the unknown id on the story unchanged; the log counts that story as `unassigned`, never under the unknown id.
- The line is emitted only when `args.agentRouting?.enabled === true` and `args.agentRouting.profiles` is non-empty, the same condition under which `resolveAgentAssignment` assigns anything.

**Integration**

Symbols read, unchanged:

- `OneShotPromptBuilder.agentCapabilityCards(profiles: AgentRoutingProfile[]): string` — renders the `Cost` column the new step refers to.
- `PlanPromptBuilder.build(specContent, codebaseContext, outputFilePath?, packages?, packageDetails?, projectProfile?, proposers?, profiles?): PlanningPromptParts` — appends `agentProfileInstruction()` when profiles are given.
- `buildDecomposePromptSync(input: DecomposePromptInput): string` — appends it through `OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfiles`.
- `finalizePrdRouting(prd, agentRouting, profileName, models, defaultAgent, only?, preserveExistingAgent?): PRD` — produces the finalized `routing.agentProfileId` values the log counts.
- `getLogger()` from `@/logger`; `Logger.info(stage: string, message: string, data?: Record<string, unknown>): void`.

**Failure Handling**

- `routing.agents` absent, `enabled: false`, or `profiles` empty: No log line; the PRD is written exactly as before.
- A counted story has no `agentProfileId` after finalization (none chosen, no default profile): Counted in `unassigned`; not an error.
- A counted story keeps an `agentProfileId` that names no configured profile (unknown id, no default profile): Counted in `unassigned`, not under that id; not an error.
- The plan model ignores the new step: No code-side correction; the pick stands as the model wrote it.

**Scope** — In: modify the existing rubric and persistence functions; add unit tests only in `packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/builders/agent-profile-rubric.test.ts` and `packages/nax/test/unit/plan/strategies/persist-prd-profile-log.test.ts`. No dependencies. Existing tests need no modifications; their rubric substrings remain unchanged. Out: no inter-story exclusions because this is the sole story. The following nearby feature boundaries remain explicit:
- `resolveOperatingTier` precedence is unchanged: a profile's tier still takes precedence over `autoMode.complexityRouting` at run time.
- No run-time selection change: the story router hook (`routing.router`) and its precedence are untouched.
- nax does not re-pick or correct the plan model's `agentProfileId` in code; the rubric is guidance to the model only.
- No skew threshold, warning or failure on the distribution; the log line is informational only.
- The capability card table (`agentCapabilityCards`) columns and the `AgentRoutingProfile` schema are unchanged; a profile with no `costTier` gets no implied cost.
- The `nax plan` run summary printed to stdout is unchanged; the distribution is in the log only.
- The `agentProfileId` field hints in the plan and decompose JSON schemas ("best-matching profile … omit if none fits") are unchanged; the numbered rubric is the procedure the model follows.

**Interface** — Existing signatures remain unchanged:

```typescript
OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfileInstruction(): string
finalizeAndWritePrd(args: PersistPrdArgs): Promise<string>
```

`OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfileInstruction(): string` (`src/prompts/builders/one-shot-builder.ts`): Target: returns the header line plus the five numbered steps shown under Approach, signature unchanged.

`finalizeAndWritePrd(args: PersistPrdArgs): Promise<string>` (`src/plan/strategies/persist-prd.ts`): Target: same signature and return value; additionally emits the `"agent profile assignment"` `info` line described under Approach, once per call, when the routing condition holds.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfileInstruction() returns text with exactly five numbered steps, 1. through 5., in that order.

[unit] Step 3 of OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfileInstruction() conditions on the story's complexity being `simple` or `medium` (naming both values), and says to also keep every profile step 1 did not eliminate whose Cost is lower than the Cost of every profile step 2 kept, even when its affinity does not list the story's task type or domain.
[unit] Step 3 of OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfileInstruction() states the cost order `low < medium < high`.
[unit] Step 3 of OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfileInstruction() says that when step 2 kept no profile, the lowest-Cost profiles step 1 did not eliminate are kept.
[unit] Step 3 of OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfileInstruction() says profiles whose Cost is `—` are ignored by the step, both as candidates and in the comparison.
[unit] Step 1 of OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfileInstruction() is `1. Eliminate any profile whose weaknesses conflict with the story.`, unchanged.
[unit] Step 2 of OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfileInstruction() is `2. Keep profiles whose strengths or affinity cover the story's main job (task type + primary domain).`, unchanged.
[unit] Step 4 of OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfileInstruction() is `4. If more than one remains, choose the LOWEST cost profile.`
[unit] Step 5 of OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfileInstruction() tells the model to omit `agentProfileId` when none clearly fit and to never invent a profile id.
[unit] When PlanPromptBuilder.build is called with one AgentRoutingProfile in its profiles argument, the returned PlanningPromptParts.taskContext includes the step 3 complexity instruction.
[unit] buildDecomposePromptSync called with one profile in input.profiles produces prompt text that includes the step 3 complexity instruction.

[unit] finalizeAndWritePrd with agentRouting { enabled: true, profiles: [a, b] } and a PRD of three stories whose routing.agentProfileId values are a, a, b calls getLogger().info exactly once with stage "plan", message "agent profile assignment" and data { storyCount: 3, byProfile: { a: 2, b: 1 }, unassigned: 0 }.
[unit] With agentRouting { enabled: true, profiles: [a] } and no default, finalizeAndWritePrd counts a story with no routing.agentProfileId in unassigned and not in byProfile; this is not an error.

[unit] With agentRouting { enabled: true, default: "a", profiles: [a, b] }, finalizeAndWritePrd counts a story whose routing.agentProfileId is the unknown id "zzz" under byProfile.a, and byProfile has no "zzz" key.

[unit] With agentRouting { enabled: true, profiles: [a] } and no default, finalizeAndWritePrd counts a story whose routing.agentProfileId is the unknown id "zzz" in unassigned, and byProfile has no "zzz" key; this is not an error.

[unit] With args.scope set to a set containing only "US-002" on a PRD of stories US-001 (profile a) and US-002 (profile b), finalizeAndWritePrd logs data { storyCount: 1, byProfile: { b: 1 }, unassigned: 0 }.
[unit] With agentRouting undefined, finalizeAndWritePrd makes no info call with message "agent profile assignment".
[unit] With agentRouting { enabled: false, profiles: [a] }, finalizeAndWritePrd makes no info call with message "agent profile assignment".
[unit] With agentRouting { enabled: true, profiles: [] }, finalizeAndWritePrd makes no info call with message "agent profile assignment".
[unit] The "agent profile assignment" line is logged through info, never through warn: with the three-story a, a, b fixture, no warn call carries that message.
[unit] When routing.agents is absent, enabled: false, or profiles is empty, finalizeAndWritePrd writes the PRD exactly as before.

[unit] Given enabled agent routing with configured profiles a (costTier low) and b (costTier medium), and a model-produced medium-complexity story with routing.agentProfileId b, when finalizeAndWritePrd writes the PRD, the written story retains routing.agentProfileId b rather than being re-picked or corrected in code.

routing.reasoning: Two localized source changes and two new Bun unit-test files use existing shared prompt and persistence seams, with clear counting/fallback rules and no new abstraction or security-sensitive behavior.

suggestedCriteria: When finalizeAndWritePrd receives an empty args.scope with enabled agent routing and nonempty profiles, it logs { storyCount: 0, byProfile: {}, unassigned: 0 }.

analysis:
Enhancement closing #2606, scoped entirely to packages/nax. Codebase-memory tools are unavailable in this session, so findings come from direct source reads and text searches. Architecture guidance was read at docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:13-40: use existing dependency injection and structured logging patterns, with Bun-native tests; no new abstractions are needed.

Current behavior and modifications: packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/one-shot-builder.ts:106-114 returns the shared four-step rubric. Modify only its instruction text: insert the specified complexity-aware step 3 and renumber the existing cost and omission steps without changing their wording. Its agentProfiles method already combines cards and this static instruction (same file:85-94), while agentCapabilityCards already renders Cost from optional costTier, using an em dash when absent (same file:125-148). The existing schema defines costTier as optional low/medium/high at packages/nax/src/config/schemas-infra.ts:92; neither schema nor table needs modification. This is model guidance, not an executable profile-selection algorithm. Weakness exclusions must remain authoritative; strictly cheaper additions apply only to simple/medium; unknown costs are excluded from both comparison and candidates; same-cost profiles must not bypass affinity. Complex/expert behavior remains unchanged.

Prompt integration and consumers: packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/plan-builder.ts:337-339 already appends the shared instruction to taskContext when cards exist. Its output schema places agentProfileId inside routing (same file:438), and requires routing.complexity (same file:177). packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/decompose-builder.ts:128-165 uses OneShotPromptBuilder.agentProfiles in both target-story and spec modes; its output examples use top-level complexity (same file:29,53). Preserve the field-agnostic phrase 'the story’s complexity' so both response formats use the identical instruction. These callers require tests, not source changes. Do not alter schema hints.

Logging integration: packages/nax/src/plan/strategies/persist-prd.ts already imports getLogger and defines PersistPrdArgs, including scope as ReadonlySet<string> (same file:77). finalizeAndWritePrd performs fidelity repair, structure enforcement, workdir canonicalization and validation, then calls finalizePrdRouting at line 320 and writes finalized JSON at line 329. Insert the single informational distribution emission between that call and the write. Count finalized.userStories, filtered by scope when provided, and recognize only ids configured in args.agentRouting.profiles. Guard with enabled === true and nonempty profiles. Use a typed count map with safe key handling, do not prepopulate unused ids, and count absent/unknown ids as unassigned. No new module or exported symbol is needed. Logger.info accepts (stage, message, data?) at packages/nax/src/logger/types.ts:60. Return outputPath and write identical PRD content as before; logging must not mutate routing.

Finalization semantics and risk: packages/nax/src/plan/strategies/finalize-routing.ts:20-66 delegates to resolveAgentAssignment, preserves out-of-scope stories by identity, and stamps selected profile/origin fields only when an assignment resolves. packages/nax/src/agents/shared/agent-profile-resolver.ts:23-43 gates on routing enabled/nonempty profiles, resolves a known selected id, falls back to the configured default, or returns null. Thus an unknown id with no default remains on the story, while an unknown id with default becomes the default id before counting. Never count an unknown raw id as a profile or add another correction path. Existing unknown-id warnings are emitted at stage routing (resolver:34-40) and must remain intact; 'never warn' applies only to the new 'agent profile assignment' message, not to unrelated warnings. Scope filtering must occur on the finalized PRD to prevent decomposition from reporting the whole existing backlog.

Persistence callers and impact: persistPrd wraps finalizeAndWritePrd at packages/nax/src/plan/strategies/persist-prd.ts:334-348. Single planning paths call that wrapper at packages/nax/src/plan/strategies/single.ts:43,57; shared write/recovery paths call it at packages/nax/src/plan/strategies/write-prd.ts:31,36,66. Decompose imports and invokes finalizeAndWritePrd at packages/nax/src/cli/plan-decompose.ts:17,201. Putting the emission at the existing persistence seam covers these paths once per persistence call without adding caller logging. No adapter, runtime router, operating-tier precedence, CLI stdout summary or cross-package changes are required. Existing PRDs/configurations need no migration, new dependency, version bump or schema change. Risks are prompt wording drift, logging pre-finalized ids, leaking unknown ids into byProfile, incorrectly counting outside scope, and global logger/dependency mocks leaking between tests.

Tests and implementation sequence: use tdd-simple, writing the two specified new Bun test files first, then changing the two existing source functions. packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/builders/one-shot-builder.test.ts:158-168 already checks weakness elimination, LOWEST cost, omit agentProfileId and never invent; all assertions survive. Existing capability-card tests at the same file:18-121 cover cost rendering and missing cost. Existing plan-builder.test.ts, decompose-builder.test.ts, finalize-routing.test.ts, persist-prd-workdir.test.ts and single.test.ts provide regression coverage around affected seams. The persistence fixture to mirror is packages/nax/test/unit/plan/strategies/persist-prd-workdir.test.ts:8-68: reuse makePRD, makeStory, makeNaxConfig().models, inject _persistPrdDeps.existsSync/discoverWorkspacePackages, capture writeFile output, and restore dependencies after every test. Its captureWarnings helper wraps only warn at line 54; add equivalent info capture in the new file and retain warn capture for the message-specific never-warn assertion. Restore logger methods in finally/afterEach; avoid module-wide mocks and unsafe casts. Test the exact rubric's numbered lines and every specified step-3 clause directly, then prove the instruction appears in PlanPromptBuilder.build().taskContext and buildDecomposePromptSync with typed nonempty profile fixtures. Capture info calls with stage/message/data and assert the exact distribution for normal, missing, unknown/default, unknown/no-default, scoped, disabled, absent and empty-profile cases. Assert disabled cases still write the PRD as before, and that the new log is observational even when the model retains a valid medium-cost pick. No live LLM, filesystem fixture tree or runtime selection tests are necessary. Targeted development command from packages/nax is bun test test/unit/prompts/builders/agent-profile-rubric.test.ts test/unit/plan/strategies/persist-prd-profile-log.test.ts --timeout=30000; automatic pipeline gates handle lint/typecheck/regressions. Existing tests are not to be edited; the spec's 'Modifies: None' refers to existing test modifications, not to the two required source edits.

Binding structure: exactly US-001, workdir packages/nax, dependencies [], medium complexity because two source edits and two new unit-test files use standard existing seams; no security-sensitive behavior or new abstraction warrants heavier isolation.

Refine audit: all 20 explicit US-001 spec criteria remain in acceptanceCriteria in spec order: (1) five numbered steps; (2) simple/medium, weakness-safe strictly-cheaper additions despite affinity mismatch; (3) low < medium < high; (4) no-affinity-match lowest-Cost fallback; (5) em-dash costs excluded from candidates and comparison; (6) unchanged weakness-elimination step; (7) unchanged affinity step; (8) exact renumbered LOWEST-cost step; (9) omission/no invented id; (10) shared instruction in the plan prompt; (11) shared instruction in decompose; (12) exact three-story info distribution; (13) absent id unassigned; (14) unknown id counted under the finalized default; (15) unknown id without default unassigned, never an unknown map key; (16) US-002-only scope; (17) absent routing suppresses log; (18) disabled routing suppresses log; (19) empty profiles suppress log; (20) informational message never emitted through warn. Regression anchors unchanged, even-when and no-unknown-key clauses are preserved. Failure-table rows map to criteria 17-19 plus 21 (unchanged writes), 13 (absent id is not an error), 15 (unknown id is not an error), and 22 (retain a model-selected configured profile instead of adding code-side correction). Criterion 10 now names the actual returned taskContext rather than implying build returns a string; criterion 22 uses a concrete written-JSON fixture instead of requiring a live model to ignore instructions. All seven feature-level exclusions remain verbatim in outOfScope and are echoed at the nearby story boundaries. All five context files match the spec and were re-read; both expected files are story outputs only. Exactly one story, its empty dependency list, workdir, medium complexity and tdd-simple strategy remain unchanged. No additional module, export, runtime selection behavior, existing-test edit or migration was introduced.
